function: Maps noisy uplink pilots (plus user weights and locations) directly to BS beamforming vectors and RIS phase shifts that maximize the downlink weighted sum-rate (p. 1, 5).
system: Downlink TDD MISO: 8-antenna BS (4x2 URA), reflecting RIS of 100 elements (10x10), K=4 users, 1.5 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth (p. 8).
method: Hypernetwork generates part of the weights of a beamforming network (FCNN or GNN) from user weights or locations; self-supervised training on weighted sum-rate loss, Adam (p. 6, 9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh direct link, Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links (4-10 dB), path loss from 3GPP 38.901 [36] only; 400 samples per iteration, 1000 new test samples (p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Same settings for training and testing on 1000 fresh samples; Fig. 6: one default-trained model tested at other noise powers and Rician factors (p. 9-11).
baselines: BCD with manifold optimization and weighted MMSE under perfect CSI; learned static-FCNN, static-GNN2 (GNN of [22]) and static-GNN3 beamforming networks (p. 6).
metrics: Average downlink weighted sum-rate (bit/sec/Hz), relative gap to BCD-perfect-CSI, number of pilots needed, training time and test runtime (p. 9-13).
complexity: Big-O expressions for static-GNN3, HNB-FCNN and HNB-GNN2; training 21.9-26.0 h; test runtime per realization 1.7 ms (HNB-FCNN), 2.8 ms (HNB-GNN2) (p. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 8: "modeled as Rician fading" for the BS-RIS and RIS-user links, with a Rayleigh direct link and i.i.d. CN(0,1) components; 3GPP [36] is cited only for the path loss (Table VI). No 3GPP fading model, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "similar results were obtained to demonstrate the robustness of the proposed HNB schemes to different Rician factors as shown in Fig. 6c"; Fig. 6c plots "HNB-GNN2-loc-default-training" over Rician factors 4-12 dB. p. 10: "generalizing to data generated using different characteristics or parameters". The noise-power tests alone are SNR sweeps.
q3_support: p. 6: "the GNN of [22]" (static-GNN2, with static-FCNN and static-GNN3) as learned baselines; "block-coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm iteratively employs manifold optimization and weighted MMSE" as non-learned baseline. p. 9: "static-FCNN, static-GNN2 and static-GNN3 schemes by 44%, 38% and 33%"; p. 10: "closes the relative performance gap to the optimistic BCD-perfect-CSI benchmark to 13%".
q4_support: p. 12: "described in terms of the number of operations", with Big-O expressions; p. 13: "required 1.7 ms and 2.8 ms" for HNB-FCNN and HNB-GNN2, against "required 1.4 ms, 2.1 ms and 4.6 ms" for the static schemes.
q5_support: p. 9: "1000 new independently generated test samples" from the paper's own simulator (p. 8); no link to code or data, no public dataset, no measured data.
notes: Included, area 3 (learned BS beamforming and RIS phase configuration from pilots, main metric weighted sum-rate). q1=0: custom Rayleigh/Rician simulator, only the path loss cites 3GPP 38.901 [36] (p. 8, Table VI). q2=1 is a judgment call resting on Fig. 6c (p. 11): a default-trained model tested over Rician factors 4-12 dB; the UL/DL noise-power tests (Fig. 6a-b) are SNR sweeps that would not count alone, and the default Rician factor is not stated, so the reviewer should confirm. q3=1: non-learned BCD with perfect CSI and learned static-FCNN/GNN2/GNN3, where static-GNN2 is the published GNN of [22] extended with a user-weight input; the static variants also act as ablations of the HNB. q4=1: Big-O expressions and runtimes (p. 12-13). q5=0: no code or data link, synthetic data. Tables I and VI and Fig. 6 were checked on the PDF pages 4, 8 and 11.
